result.title: Gaze World Model
result.summary: Where a person looks indicates their focus of attention, and how their gaze shifts between targets reveals how that attention responds to a changing scene. Existing gaze target estimation methods largely operate frame by frame and do not model these shifts. Gaze shifts are often driven by dynamic changes in the scene, which is the kind of information world models are designed to encode. This relationship is subtle, however, since an event far across the frame may produce only a slight movement of the person's head or eyes. We therefore introduce the Gaze World Model (GWM), which co-trains latent scene prediction with person-conditioned gaze supervision on a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder; in our ablations, the latent prediction objective improves both shift detection and gaze localization. Given a video clip and the person's head box, GWM estimates gaze locations and detects gaze shifts in the observed clip, and forecasts future gaze and shifts from predicted scene features. To train and evaluate these tasks, we augment VideoAttentionTarget and ChildPlay with event-level gaze-shift annotations. GWM achieves state-of-the-art shift detection on these benchmarks, about 10 points higher in four-class AP than the strongest baseline, while remaining comparable to the strongest image-based models in gaze target estimation, and outperforms the compared baselines on future gaze localization and shift forecasting.

AI.brief_summary: 在冻结的 V-JEPA 2.1 编码器上联合训练 latent 场景预测与人条件化的注视监督，用于视频中的注视点估计、注视转移检测以及基于预测场景特征的未来注视预测，并为基准补充事件级注视转移标注。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「latent 预测目标经消融可同时提升转移检测与注视定位」的辅助训练线索，可供核查 LVR 中预测式辅助目标与视觉证据定位/筛选的关系；但本文研究对象是人类注视而非模型自身的推理状态，与主线仍有距离。
